title: Point restriction on whole strict Roos cones and its localization
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Set $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, let $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], and on the small pro-etale site set $B_n=(A_n)_s$ and $\widehat R_s=\lim_nB_n$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $\mathscr S_s$ be the abelian category of strict $B_n$-module systems with quotient-linear transitions, with its ordinary unbounded derived category [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $U_s$ for levelwise restriction to $\widehat R_s$-module towers and $\mathcal L_s=R\lim U_s$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Put $F_r=(h^r)^{-1}$ on module complexes with scalars transported through the canonical coefficient isomorphisms, and $G_r$ for its levelwise functor on systems [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image, def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Read the finite levels through $j_{r,M}:F_rM\to(h^r)^*M$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, of part (a) of the latter definition. Let $\Gamma_\bullet$ be restriction of scalars followed by exact sections levelwise, retaining all transitions [def-trf-coefficient-tower-operations, lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact].

For any strict tower complex $V$ put $P_V=\prod_{n\geq1}V_n$, $s_V((v_n)_n)=(t_nv_{n+1})_n$, and
$$H(V)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_V)[-1],\qquad H(V)^i=P_V^{i-1}\oplus P_V^i,\qquad d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_V)a,da).$$
Use total right derived inverse limit and its normalized strict Roos comparison [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], whose strict augmentation is $z\mapsto(0,(\gamma_nz)_n)$.

Fix $r\geq1$. Set $T=\Gamma(s,-)$ with constant-section $R$-action. For every unbounded completed-module complex $K$, let $\sigma_{r,K}:TK\to TF_rK$ be restriction along $h^r$, followed by the inverse-image colimit insertion and sheafification [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport, lem-weil-point-automorphism-restriction-natural]. Thus in site-reindexing coordinates it is actual restriction from $K(s,\mathrm{id})$ to $K(s,h^r)$. This is an $R$-linear natural chain transformation, localizing to all ambient derived complexes; in particular it is defined on $\mathcal L_sC$ without completeness or boundedness assumptions.

For a complex $M$ of strict coefficient systems put $X=U_sM$, $Y=U_sG_rM$, and take the actual strict map $u=u_{r,M}:T^{\operatorname{Tow}}X\to T^{\operatorname{Tow}}Y$ and its localization $I_{r,[M]}$ [lem-trf-point-system-transport-descent]. Let $\kappa^F_X:F_rH(X)\to H(Y)$ and $\kappa^T_V:T H(V)\to H(T^{\operatorname{Tow}}V)$, for $V=X,Y$, denote the canonical isomorphisms applying the product comparison on both coordinates, with the finite-level identifications $j_r$ for $F_r$ [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit]. Write $P=\prod_nu_{r,n}$ and $s,s'$ for the shifts of the section towers. Then the following are identities of actual chain maps:
$$(1-s')P=P(1-s),\qquad H(u)(b,a)=(Pb,Pa),$$
$$(\kappa^T_Y)^{-1}H(u)=T(\kappa^F_X)\sigma_{r,H(X)}(\kappa^T_X)^{-1}.$$
In every degree both coordinates of this last identity, after the canonical product comparisons and finite $j_r$ identifications, send $(x_n)_n$ to $(x_n|_{h^r})_n$. In particular the equality includes the shifted-product coordinate and has no off-diagonal term.

For the normalized total-limit identifications $\eta_V:R\lim T^{\operatorname{Tow}}V\xrightarrow{\sim}H(T^{\operatorname{Tow}}V)$ one has
$$\eta_Y R\lim(I_{r,[M]})=H(u)\eta_X.$$
The entire strict square is natural in strict chain maps, commutes with inverted quasi-isomorphisms, and is independent of the chosen strict representative under the normalized comparison maps. These are whole-tower identities; equality of derived morphisms is not inferred from equality after evaluation at individual levels.

proof.text: Postcompose each diagonal comparison with its nth product projection. The product_projection equation gives both requested coordinate identities. Naturality of roosF with respect to the coefficient identification gives the corresponding kappaF identities after composing with that identification. Its sectionwise identity implies equality of the underlying module structures, so cancellation gives precisely the stated heterogeneous equalities of actual linear maps.

source.place: Clause (3): integral morphisms are derived limits of levelwise composites; explicit agent-written point-restriction refinement

proof.text: The restriction of U(M) to the nth vertical slice is the actual finite scalar restriction by coefficientSequenceRestriction_evaluation. Its underlying abelian presheaf is therefore the original presheaf at (n,-). Thus ambient raw restriction and the specified HasRestrictionComponents formula coincide. Together with coefficient_sections this identifies u followed by the coefficient map with sigma at every degree and level.

source.place: Clause (3): integral morphisms are derived limits of levelwise composites; explicit agent-written point-restriction refinement

proof.text: Cancel the sections comparison isomorphisms, then test the two maps to the Roos cone against both families of product projections. Naturality of roosF gives the projections of H(u); the preceding level equation, the comparison projection equations and naturality of sigma identify them with the projections of T(kappaF) after sigma. Product and biproduct extensionality give equality of actual chain maps. The transition and diagonal assertions follow from roosU_natural and roosF_map_chi. Exact products from the simultaneous data and roos_map_quasiIso give quasi-isomorphism preservation.

source.place: Clause (3): integral morphisms are derived limits of levelwise composites; explicit agent-written point-restriction refinement

proof.text: Apply normalizedRoosIso to scalar modules and the universal right-derived limit unit, composed with the canonical ordinary-limit interchange isomorphism. On K-injectives the unit is invertible. The resulting inverse eta has the required normalization on every complex by its defining equation and cancellation of the interchange isomorphism. Finally the representative equation for derivedTransport, the factor isomorphism identities and naturality of eta give the displayed total-limit transport identity.
